verdict.rationale: Greptile's security page says customers can turn off logging and make chats 100% private, and self-hosted deployments keep logs on customer servers only (greptile-supp-1). The same page, however, reserves the right to aggregate and anonymize customer data for analytics and AI training, with no documented opt-out (greptile-supp-2). So the opt-out covers chat logging, or requires self-hosting, rather than usage tracking generally. Missing for 10: an explicit telemetry/usage-analytics opt-out control for the hosted service, an opt-out from de-identified analytics and AI training, CLI/MCP telemetry settings, and independent corroboration.
